jobs.occupation: Product Manager – Notifications | Help Dalux Users Focus on What Matters
jobs.description:
Product Manager – Notifications | Help Dalux Users Focus on What Matters

Construction projects generate an enormous amount of information. Files change. Tasks are assigned. Deadlines approach. Comments are added. Reviews require action. Issues are reported. People are mentioned. Workflows progress. But more information does not necessarily make people better informed.

Dalux is looking for a Product Manager to take dedicated ownership of Notifications and help us answer a deceptively difficult product question:

How do we make sure users know what requires their attention – without overwhelming them with information?

Notifications exist throughout our products today, across email, mobile, and in-product experiences. As Dalux has grown, so has their complexity. We believe this area deserves dedicated product ownership and a coherent strategy across our products.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Notification Strategy: Define a coherent product direction for how Dalux communicates important events and required actions to users.

• Product Discovery: Understand when users need to be informed, when they need to take action, and when a notification simply creates unnecessary noise.

• Customer Insights: Research how different users manage information and attention across complex projects and busy working days.

• Cross-product Ownership: Map and improve notification experiences across Dalux products rather than optimizing individual notifications in isolation.

• Channels & Preferences: Develop experiences spanning in-app notifications, email, mobile push, notification preferences, subscriptions, following, mentions, reminders, and digests.

• Relevance & Prioritization: Explore grouping, prioritization, timing, and deduplication to ensure important information stands out.

• Actionability: Make notifications useful by ensuring users understand why they received them, what has changed, and what action they should take.

• Product Analytics: Use quantitative and qualitative insights to understand which notifications create value and which create noise.

• Shared Capabilities: Work with Development and other Product Managers to create common notification principles and platform capabilities that can be reused across Dalux.

About You

You probably don't currently have "Notifications Product Manager" as your job title – and that's perfectly fine.

We're looking for an experienced Product Manager who finds the underlying problem interesting and has the product and systems thinking required to solve it.

We believe you:

• Have strong Product Management experience, preferably from B2B SaaS, collaboration, productivity, workflow, communication, or similar software.

• Have excellent product discovery and UX instincts.

• Think systematically and can turn many individual use cases into coherent product concepts.

• Understand the tension between keeping users informed and creating notification fatigue.

• Are comfortable owning a horizontal capability spanning multiple products and development teams.

• Can combine user research with product analytics to understand behavior.

• Care about interaction details and understand how seemingly small product decisions can have a large cumulative impact on user experience.

• Can simplify complex systems involving events, recipients, relevance, timing, preferences, and communication channels.

• Communicate fluently in English, written and spoken.

Construction Technology Experience Is Welcome But Not Required .

Experience from collaboration, communication, workflow, or productivity software would be particularly relevant.

What To Expect At Dalux

At Dalux, you'll join a product-driven company where ideas quickly become reality and where you'll have a direct impact on the products we build.

We offer:

• A collaborative and informal work environment with flat hierarchies

• High ownership, trust, and the freedom to drive initiatives

• Talented and dedicated colleagues in an international team

• A central Copenhagen office, flexible work hours, and no dress code

• Monthly social events and an active community

• Attractive benefits including health insurance, lunch, fitness facilities, and free parking

• Opportunities for professional growth and development

Ready for the next step?

We are reviewing applications on an ongoing basis, so please submit your resume and application as soon as possible.

About Dalux

Founded in 2005, Dalux is a Danish Contech company revolutionizing the construction industry with innovative software built on geometric processing and 3D computer graphics.

Over the past years, we’ve grown by 40% annually and now have over 900 employees across 50+ offices in more than 25 countries. All product development takes place in our Østerbro, Copenhagen office, where we focus on building the future of construction technology. We place great value on our strong social community and close collaboration with colleagues, which is why we primarily work from our Copenhagen location.

Application deadline:

As soon as possible

****About The Role

**We are looking for an experienced financial-crime leader to be our registered MLRO / Hvidvaskansvarlig (HVL

• 7, stk. 2) for Monta Pay ApS under our EMI license and to lead Financial Crime Prevention (FCP) across Monta, group-wide for the Danish/EEA EMI plus UK and US compliance as those markets scale. The role is registered with Finanstilsynet, so the appointment is subject to a fit & proper assessment as a change of key function holder.

**

Propose the risk appetite and risk-based approach for Board approval and monitor against it, and keep the framework effective and proportionate to our activities, customer types (B2B & B2C), and transaction flows.

Set the rules, thresholds and procedures the Financial Operations team runs in the first line, and assure their quality and effectiveness.

• Sanctions & screening: Set the screening standards (lists, thresholds, re-screening frequency) and assure the quality of first-line alert handling.

• Policy suite, risk assessment & governance: Maintain the AML/CFT policy suite in the Centralised Policy Register (with version control and Board-approval tracking), and own the Business-Wide Risk Assessment (BWRA) and the AML risk assessment underpinning the framework.

• Regulatory reporting: Deliver AML and payments regulatory reporting (for example Section 99 Payment Act, KPSD, AML/CTF returns) and ensure CESOP readiness.

• On AML: everything required to obtain the EMI license has been submitted and approved. The remaining gap is operational readiness, and that is the focus: embedding the framework in day-to-day operations and rolling it out with our customers and with colleagues across Monta.

• On FCP: This role brings centralised ownership and direction, consolidating what already exists, formalising it into clear Standard Operating Procedures, and training the relevant teams on them ahead of go-live.

• Concrete early priorities include standing up transaction monitoring and fraud detection, locking v1.0 of the policy suite (Sanctions, PEP, EDD, Outsourcing, and the Sanction-Screening and SAR/STR filing SOPs) into the Centralised Policy Register, building the regulatory-reporting data structure and CESOP readiness, finalising KYC/KYB (EU + US), and securing your Finanstilsynet fit & proper approval ahead of go-live. A structured focus-areas plan accompanies this role.

**Requirements

**

Comparable experience in public authorities, AML consulting, or other AML-regulated sectors (for example gaming/gambling) will also be considered.

• Strong, current understanding of Danish AML law (Hvidvaskloven) and the EU framework (AMLD/AMLR, EBA guidelines), plus sanctions regimes. Awareness of the incoming EU AML package (AMLR + AMLD6, applying July 2027) is a plus.

• Experience across risk controls, compliance, the payments area, credit management, or lines-of-defence leadership. Fintech/scale-up experience is a plus.

• Strong communication skills, autonomy, and sound decision-making, with the ability to build from a blank page and then scale a function and team.

• Analytical and investigative skills to detect patterns and anomalies in financial transactions and to investigate suspicious activity.

• Danish speaking, or willing to learn (the role is regulator-facing).

• Relevant education (economics, mathematics, law, or financial-sector training) is a plus.

• No prior convictions or legal issues that would make the candidate unfit for the role, particularly offences related to financial crime, fraud, money laundering, or other criminal activities undermining trust and integrity.

_If this sounds like you, we look forward to receiving your application.

_Why Monta

• Impact, not easy mode — your work matters, and you’ll feel it every day.

• Ownership from day one — we don’t micromanage, we expect you to deliver.

• The grind is real — priorities shift, and flexibility is sometimes needed to get things across the finish line. But so are the rewards: impact, growth, and a team that has your back.

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**The Role & Department

**The role is a senior quality specialist responsible for GMP quality oversight of commercial Drug Substance (DS) and Biological Intermediates (BI) manufactured at external Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs). The role is based in Denmark and reports to the Director of QA Commercial – Drug Substance & Intermediates.

You will be part of an experienced and highly skilled QA organization, with this position holding primary accountability for Drug Substance and Biological Intermediates across commercial supply chains. The role interfaces closely with CMOs, partners, and internal subject matter experts across Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Technical Operations, and Supply Chain.

**Key Responsibilities

**_**General Compliance

**_

• Lead QA representation for Drug Substance and Biological Intermediate in cross-functional Genmab project groups and key external collaborations, providing expert input and ensuring alignment with QA governance and regulatory expectations

• Act as a QA subject matter expert on GMP for biologics Drug Substance and Biological Intermediates, providing expert guidance, supporting resolution of complex quality issues, and ensuring consistent application of quality standards

• Gain and maintain expert knowledge of applicable GMP legislation, guidelines, and industry practices relevant to DS and BI manufacturing; assess relevance for Genmab activities and ensure structured dissemination of applicable updates to relevant stakeholders

• Lead the resolution of DS- and BI-related quality issues in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders, escalating critical or high-risk matters as appropriate to ensure timely and compliant decision-making

_Pharmaceutical Quality System (PQS)

_

• Continuously improving PQS: Participate in developing, maintaining, and continuously improving Genmab’s Pharmaceutical Quality System (PQS) in alignment with applicable GMP and GDP requirements

• Quality Risk Management: Apply and support quality risk management principles in complex PQS activities, providing expert input to risk assessments and mitigation actions

• Procedures: Review/authoring and approval of SOPs, Work Instructions, templates and forms within assigned areas, and support document updates in accordance with the PQS

• Deviation, CAPA, Change Control: Handle and support deviations, CAPAs and change controls, providing expert input and ensuring compliance with procedures and applicable regulatory requirements

• Inspections & Audits: Participate in audits and inspections performed by national authorities and internal or external auditors as required. Support audit and inspection readiness by ensuring documentation, procedures and processes within assigned scope are maintained in compliance with company standards and applicable regulations. Support audit and inspection preparation and conduct through back-office activities, documentation and presentation support

• QMR: Provide expert input to Quality Management Reviews (QMRs) as part of the PQS, contributing to data analysis, trend interpretation and identification of quality risks and improvement opportunities

• Complaints & Recalls: Handle and support complex product complaints and recall-related activities as part of the PQS, providing expert input to investigations, risk assessments and corrective actions in compliance with procedures and regulatory requirements

• Batch Review & Release: Perform batch review and batch release activities and act as delegated QP and ensure compliance with approved procedures and regulatory requirements

• CPV: Support, review and approve Continued Process Verification (CPV) activities as part of the PQS, providing expert input to data analysis, trend evaluation and identification of potential process risks in compliance with regulatory requirements

• APQR: Prepare, review and support complex Annual Product Quality Reviews (APQRs) as part of the PQS, providing expert input to data analysis, trend evaluation and conclusions in compliance with regulatory requirements

• Training: Provide expert training in complex or specialized quality topics as defined by QA, supporting consistent understanding and application of quality requirements

_Supplier Quality Oversight

_

• Provide expert and operational supplier quality oversight for Drug Substance and Biological Intermediate manufacturers, including supplier audits, vendor risk evaluations, Quality Agreements, supplier meetings, and external notifications

• Provide expert input to the resolution of complex DS- and BI-related supplier quality issues, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements and Genmab quality standards

**Requirements

**

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant life science discipline

• Solid experience (5 years) within pharmaceutical QA GMP, preferably related to Drug Substance and Intermediates

• Experience with outsourced manufacturing and delegated QP responsibilities

• Strong communication and collaboration skills; fluent in English

• Ability to work independently in a complex and fast-paced environment

• Ability to thrive in a fast-paced and changing environment

• Results-oriented and committed to contributing to Genmab’s overall success

DKK607.920,00---911.880,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**Benefits

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

**

• Monitor and assess new and changing regulatory requirements relevant to Veo and help determine their practical implications for our products and business.

• Contribute to the continued development of Veo's broader GRC framework and take part in cross-functional compliance projects as required.

**

• Relevant professional experience within product compliance, regulatory compliance, certification, quality/regulatory affairs or a similar area, preferably from an international company.

• An ability to understand complex regulatory requirements and translate them into practical requirements for technical, operational and commercial teams.

• Strong project and stakeholder management skills, with experience coordinating initiatives across different functions and areas of expertise.

• A structured approach to documentation, monitoring and follow-up, combined with the ability to identify and prioritize material compliance risks.

• Strong business understanding and a pragmatic approach to compliance. You should be comfortable finding solutions that meet regulatory requirements while enabling the business to operate effectively.

• Comfortable working independently and taking ownership in an environment where processes and frameworks are still being developed.

• Strong communication skills and professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

At Veo, the Governance, Risk & Compliance team provides oversight, coordination and assurance across the company. We work closely with teams throughout Veo to ensure that regulatory requirements and risks are identified, appropriately owned and effectively managed.

You will report to the Head of Governance, Risk & Compliance and will have considerable opportunity to shape how Veo approaches compliance as the company continues to grow.

With an IoT platform connecting more millions of devices, and growing - Trackunit is building the connectivity layer underneath the construction industry. Every one of those units carries a cellular radio, and every one of those radios sits inside a web of standards, type approvals, and patent licences that decides whether we can ship and where we can ship.

You will join our IoT Division, Device Reliability Engineering (DRE) team as an expert on IoT certifications, standards, and licensing including Standard Essential Patents (SEP). This position shapes both our exposure and our coverage arguments, and it means this role works in every direction at once, with suppliers, regulatory approvals, legal advisors, product and engineering, and with customers.

This is a role for someone who can hold a genuinely complex domain in their head and then explain it in three sentences to a customer who has never heard the phrase “patent exhaustion.”

Experience level: a deep specialist role. We expect solid, hands-on experience with cellular device approvals and licensing — likely 10+ years across regulatory, certification, or IP/licensing work in mobile, IoT, or telecom hardware. This is a senior individual contributor position with no direct reports, high autonomy, and direct executive visibility.

With locations in the heart of Copenhagen, Kolding, Aarhus, and Aalborg, we offer a flexible setup with the possibility to work from one of our locations — or remotely from anywhere in Denmark.

****What's in it for you?

• A domain you will own, not administer. IoT Cellular License, SEP and certification strategy is an executive-level topic at Trackunit right now, with real financial exposure attached. You will not be filing paperwork in a corner, you will be shaping the position the company takes.

• International environment with regular check-ins and social events across teams, departments and borders.

• We take your personal and professional development goals seriously and we support them through training, coaching, and mindfulness as well as with an open feedback culture to enable you to identify your strengths and opportunities.

• Flexibility and hybrid working is not just a cliché to us or something we state in a job posting. We offer a flexible setup because we believe you know best how to structure your work. Once you have chosen how you work best, let us know what you need: we got you covered with the IT equipment you need for your work.

• Turning the Tide. At Trackunit, we aim to create and contribute to an inclusive workplace. And this priority starts with our hiring — we do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity, sexual orientation, personal expression, ethnicity, religious belief, or disability status. We only assess candidates on their qualifications and merit. Learn more about TIDE and other DE&I initiatives here.

****What you'll do

****Your work splits roughly into four parts: licensing, approvals, guidance, and governance.

• Own our SEP position. Understand where our cellular SEP exposure actually sits across our device portfolio, track the relevant patent pools and licensing programmes, and maintain a clear, evidence-based view of what is covered through our supply chain and what is not.

• Run supplier licensing due diligence. Establish and maintain a consistent set of asks across module suppliers — coverage confirmation, standards and generations covered, and honest disclosure of known gaps — so responses can be compared side by side and fed into supplier qualification.

• Support licensing negotiations and claims. Work alongside our General Counsel, external patent counsel, and economic advisors on royalty basis questions, valuation and apportionment arguments, and claims that reach us through our OEM customers. You bring the technical and supply chain substance; they bring the legal strategy.

• Own global type approvals and certification. Plan and steer RED/CE, FCC, ISED, UKCA, and the wider set of regional approvals, plus GCF/PTCRB and carrier certification, across a multi-region device portfolio. Keep certification on the critical path of new product programmes rather than at the end of them.

• Stay ahead of regulatory change. Cyber Resilience Act, RED delegated acts, radio spectrum and network sunsets, environmental and product compliance requirements — know what is coming, when it bites, and what it means for our roadmap.

• Make the complex simple, and guide without over-promising. Write and maintain the internal playbooks, customer-facing explainers, and OEM guidance that turn this domain into something a commercial colleague or a customer can act on. Be the person Sales, Legal, and customers come to when a licensing notification lands, explaining the landscape accurately, saying clearly where the limits of our position are, and pointing customers to independent specialist advice where that is the right answer.

• Build the governance. Response protocols, decision records, escalation paths, and embedding licensing and compliance requirements into how we qualify suppliers and run the product development lifecycle.

****Who you are

****We think you'll need

• Strong working knowledge of cellular connectivity (e.g. LTE-M, NB-IoT, LTE Cat-1/1bis, 5G) and the direction of travel, plus a real understanding of the module and chipset landscape.

• Solid, practical experience with licensing and Standard Essential Patents in mobile or IoT devices: FRAND principles, patent pools, patent exhaustion and the limits of sublicensing, and how royalties are actually structured and argued.

• Hands-on experience with global type approvals and regulatory certification for radio products — RED/CE, FCC, and the regional approvals that come with selling hardware worldwide.

• Experience working across a hardware supply chain with module suppliers, test houses, notified bodies, and certification partners.

• Communication as a core skill, not a bonus. You can take a genuinely complicated subject and land it in plain language, in writing, with an audience that has no background in it.

• The judgement to know what we can and cannot say to a customer, and the discipline to hold that line even when it would be easier not to.

**What Matters More Than The Checklist

**

• You are honest about uncertainty. In this domain, no one can offer a blanket guarantee, and the people who claim otherwise create problems later. We would rather be accurate than reassuring.

• You are curious and self-driven, this is a field that changes constantly, and nobody is going to hand you a reading list.

• You finish things. A clear one-page answer delivered this week beats a perfect analysis that arrives after the decision was made.

• You are comfortable being the only person in the room who knows a subject, and you use that position to make others smarter rather than to make yourself indispensable.

On AI: experience with AI tooling is not a requirement, but a strong motivation and interest in working with it is. We already use AI in our daily engineering work, including MCP servers and agents against our own platform, and we see clear potential in applying it to research, documentation, and compliance workflows. We don't expect you to have experience with this but we do expect curiosity and a willingness to learn.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries this is what we're looking for ideally, but if you're excited about this role and your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply.

****How you'll grow here

****This is a specialist role with an unusually wide view of the business, and we've set it up that way on purpose.

• Executive proximity. You will work closely with the SVP of IoT Division, while reporting into a central function for IoT, as the Device Reliability Engineering. You will help in presenting to executive leadership on exposure, risk, and recommendations. Your analysis will inform on a product technical matter (Not Legal) but with real financial and commercial decisions.

• Cross-functional reach. Legal, Finance, Product Management, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Sales all depend on this domain. Few roles at Trackunit touch as many parts of the company.

• External network. You will work with external patent counsel, economic consultants, module suppliers, certification bodies, and industry forums — building a network that extends well beyond Trackunit.

• Room to define the function. This discipline is being built out now. What it becomes — and whether it grows into a team — is substantially yours to shape.

**Coming Together To Connect Construction

**We're committed to construction one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products — it's a way of life at Trackunit. We're proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues get together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do it to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

• Executing projects within your area in close collaboration with your team, identifying risks and implementing mitigation measures.

• Focusing on overall project planning, ensuring delivery quality, and planning the necessary resources to maintain schedule and cost targets.

• Estimating costs and planning budgets in collaboration with our engineers and specialists.

• Managing project scope and ensuring that changes are analysed and agreed upon with stakeholders.

**Who You Are

**We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you:

• Work across the boundaries and you like to work in a diverse and international environment

• Create results through efficient project management and communication, leveraging from your relations to your team and stakeholder

• Have a personal commitment, known for your effectiveness and an open management style and know the impotency to win as a team

• Are fluent in English both written and spoken

**What You Bring To The Role

**To be successful in this role, we expect you to have the following experience and educational background:

• An educational background at bachelor's level or a similar relevant technical background.

• 6–10 years of experience with a proven track record in DCS and ECS/PLC Process Automation projects, preferably within the pharmaceutical industry.

• Experience with GMP project execution and preferable knowledge with S88 and S95

• Experience in executing Process Automation projects in collaboration with other disciplines, such as mechanical and process design, as well as end users.

• Experience with on-site commissioning activities, including FAT, SAT, and UAT.

• Project Management certification, e.g. PMP or PRINCE2, is preferred.

If you do not meet all the requirements, you are still welcome to apply and provide alternative experience that you believe would be valuable in this role.
